basis: Developmental delay and movement abnormalities define the syndrome; esotropia occurs in 30-79%. Minor facial and ear dysmorphism does not establish additional functional damage.
Inherited dissection directly damages cervical arteries; associated stroke is a separately diagnosed complication.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with globozoospermia affects reproduction; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the exocrine pancreas; secondary diabetes is a separately diagnosed disease.
Viral infection of the conjunctiva with conjunctival hemorrhage.
Inherited red-cell membrane disorder causing hemolytic anemia; pseudohyperkalemia is an artifact rather than systemic electrolyte disease.
Bacteria-associated destructive periodontal disease affects gingiva, dental attachment and alveolar supporting tissues.
Psychiatric preoccupation with illness without established damage to an organ axis.
Benign smooth-muscle tumor arising in the rectum; smooth-muscle histology does not imply skeletal-muscle disease.
Acute ischemic injury of the intestine; a specific arterial or venous disorder is not established by this umbrella diagnosis.
Skeletal dysplasia, retinal degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss define it; intellectual disability and brain abnormalities are core diagnostic features.
Salivary glands are the usual origin of myoepithelial carcinoma. This umbrella also includes breast and soft-tissue tumors; additional sites are not generalized.
Skeletal dysplasia and microtia define it; anal atresia and ASD each occur in 2/3. Skin aplasia (2/3), brain and urinary anomalies (~1/3) omitted by cap.
Mitochondrial defect with defining cardioencephalopathy; muscle COX deficiency in 9/9 and myopathic EMG in 3/3. Ocular and hearing abnormalities omitted by cap.
Broad thoracic neoplasm umbrella including lung and pleural tumors; pulmonary is a provisional regional assignment because other subtypes arise in different tissues.
Interferonopathy with acro-osteolysis and defining aortic calcification (5/7); glaucoma in 10/11. Psoriasiform skin disease (7/11) omitted by cap.
HHV8-associated sarcoma typically involving skin; nodal and visceral involvement varies across endemic forms and is not generalized.
Poorly characterized modifier concept; its name and sole phenotype identify nervous-system dysfunction, with no evidence for other organs.
Excess leukocytes in urine defines a urinary-system abnormality; infection and systemic blood-cell disease are not established.
Benign epidermal skin neoplasm.
Congenital structural malformation of the mitral valve.
Peroxisome biogenesis defect; brain dysfunction, liver disease and retinal dysfunction are each common (>30%) across Zellweger spectrum. Common hearing loss omitted by cap.
Defining blistering and erosions affect intertriginous skin and esophagus; common dental enamel defects also support gastrointestinal involvement.
Generalized dermal mucin deposition and sclerodermoid infiltration; no established common extracutaneous damage for this specific form.
Hereditary tumor syndrome defined by cutaneous melanoma and exocrine pancreatic cancer; other associated tumor risks do not establish additional involvement.
